R02.text: Across 28 baseline and 14 window days with full wear, most metrics were stable. Sleep averaged ~471 min (baseline) vs ~468 min (window), ending consistently at 07:00. Steps averaged ~8066 vs ~7954. Activity (~55 min), low movement (~451 min), and RHR (~56 bpm) were unchanged. RMSSD mean fell from 45.3 to 43.1 ms, driven by a single weekend drop to 23 ms on Apr 5; otherwise it stayed near 43–47 ms. Baseline RMSSD variance was very low (1.6); window variance rose to 32.8 due to that outlier.

R03.text: In your recent 14 days, sleep averaged ~468 min, about 3 min below your 28-day baseline (~471), still ending consistently at 07:00 with starts shifting ~3 min later. Steps dipped slightly (~7,954 vs ~8,066); activity minutes held near ~55. Resting heart rate was marginally lower (~55.8 vs ~56.3 bpm). Notably, HRV RMSSD dropped to ~43 ms from ~45 ms, driven by a single isolated reading of 23 ms on Apr 5; excluding it, the average returns near baseline. Variability otherwise remained typical.

R05.text: Your 14-day window closely matched your 28-day baseline. Sleep averaged ~468 min vs ~471 min, with a consistent 07:00 wake time and slightly later bedtimes (~3 min). Steps (~7,954 vs ~8,066) and active minutes (~55) were stable. Resting heart rate dipped slightly to ~55.8 bpm. HRV RMSSD was mostly steady (~43 ms), but one night dropped to 23 ms before returning; this isolated reading may reflect measurement variability. Day-to-day patterns remained consistent.

R07.text: Over 28 baseline days, sleep averaged 471 min (start ~22:50, end fixed 07:00), steps ~8066, activity ~55 min, RHR ~56 bpm, RMSSD ~45 ms. In the 14-day window, patterns remained stable: sleep -3 min, steps -112, activity unchanged, RHR -0.5 bpm. One isolated RMSSD drop to 23 ms on Apr 5 recovered to 43 ms next day; window RMSSD variance rose. Weekday/weekend structure and evening activity timing persisted. No lagged activity-sleep or same-day RHR-RMSSD relationships were evident.

R08.text: Across 28 baseline and 14 window days with full wear, most metrics stayed stable. Sleep averaged ~471 min (baseline) vs ~468 min (window), always ending at 07:00; sleep start shifted ~3 min later. Steps (~8066 vs ~7954), activity (~55 min both), low movement (~451 vs ~453 min), and resting HR (~56.3 vs ~55.8 bpm) changed minimally. However, RMSSD dropped from a stable ~45.3 ms to ~43.1 ms, driven by an isolated value of 23 ms on Apr 5 that returned to 43 ms the next day; excluding it, window RMSSD was ~44.6 ms. Paired correlations remained weak throughout.
